problem: Graph-based VLN planners such as DUET rely on attention networks whose memory cost grows with long sequences, creating a trade-off between memory efficiency and navigation reasoning.
motivation: Long-horizon navigation needs long-sequence dependency modeling and topological reasoning, but attention is memory-heavy. Structured state space models (Mamba-style) are efficient, and combining them with graph neural networks might keep topological reasoning while cutting memory.
key_idea: Integrate graph neural networks into a bidirectional selective state space model (replacing attention) so the agent reasons over the topological map efficiently, with position embeddings capturing spatial context and residual fusion of the bidirectional features.
insight: Only the abstract was available, so no ablations can be cited. The abstract claims that a graph-aware state space model can replace attention, with only a modest memory saving (4.45% GPU memory reduction versus DUET).
method: Graph-aware reasoning (GAR): graph neural networks are integrated into the state space model to model long-sequence dependencies and find topological paths from instructions and environment interaction.
Bidirectional selective state space model: scans in both directions to make the agent aware of spatial information, without attention networks.
Position embedding: captures context information in images in place of attention.
Bidirectional feature fusion with residual connection: fuses forward and backward state space features and compresses and refines fine-grained image features.

setting.backbone: DUET-style graph planner with a graph-aware bidirectional selective state space model (trained)
